key_insight: A MicroUS-specific foundation model ({micro}FM) pretrained on 1.7M unlabeled prostate ultrasound images improved data-efficient segmentation and lesion localization, especially when labeled data were scarce.
clinical_relevance: This could lower annotation burden and accelerate development of automated tools for prostate cancer imaging and biopsy guidance in MicroUS workflows.
method: Self-supervised DINOv2-style pretraining on 1,736,391 unlabeled MicroUS images from 780 patients
Fine-tuning on three downstream tasks: prostate capsule segmentation, urethra segmentation, and cancer lesion localization
Compared against random initialization and foundation models pretrained on natural, medical, and ultrasound images
evidence_signal: With only 10% of training scans, {micro}FM reached 93.8% Dice for capsule segmentation and 58.4% for urethra segmentation, and achieved about 0.75 sensitivity at 2 false positives per 3D volume for lesion localization.
watch_item: Results come from retrospective, largely single-institution pretraining and the model does not include explicit 3D modeling, so external validation is needed before broader deployment.
paper_title: Data-Efficient Prostate Micro-Ultrasound Image Analysis using a Modality-specific Foundation Model
